events.title: Purity Politics & Punishment
events.excerpt: Across our social justice movements, identity politics and purity politics have come to shape the ways in which we relate with each other, in often punitive ways...
events.description:
Across our social justice movements, identity politics and purity politics have come to shape the ways in which we relate with each other, in often punitive ways. It becomes tough to stay in connection with people who we see as wrong, bad, or harmful because of something they might have done that we morally disagree with. This can be both a simplistic and destructive way of dealing with the complexities of coexisting and resisting. But what happens to our relationships and movements if we continue to cancel anyone and everyone who falls short of a perfectionism that no-one can ever live up to?

In the face identity, purity, and punishment, this workshop offers an educational conversation about the ways we can practice accountability that deals with aggression or transgression through a process of safety, repair, and prevention – while also remaining committed to the principles of shared humanity and solidarity and the possibility of lasting change and transformation. We’ll get clear on important distinctions such as hurt vs harm, safety vs discomfort, fairness vs transaction, control vs care – and why they really matter when navigating relational breakdowns. Ultimately this conversation is about taking a look at the ways in which we unintentionally recreate the same cycles of violence and dehumanisation that we say we are fighting against, even when we’re on the “right side” or doing it for the “right reasons” – the outcome remains the same. This workshop plants a seed of commitment to creating different outcomes.

events.title: Making the Israel-Palestine Issue Open to Discussion
events.excerpt: Palestine and Israel is a topic that deeply affects many people, while also being discussed in highly emotional and often controversial ways. This space aims to make the subject approachable through empathy....
events.description:
The issue of Palestine and Israel is on many people’s minds. We want to make it possible to discuss this topic with empathy by creating a space for sharing, reflection, and listening—a space where thoughts and feelings are welcome. In doing so, we’ll explore the following questions: How did my perspective on the Palestine-Israel issue develop? Why is the Palestine-Israel issue discussed so controversially and emotionally in Germany? How can “being in the here and now” be understood in a political context? How does our powerlessness regarding this issue manifest itself—and how can we transform it into a counterforce, into the capacity to act?

This space requires a willingness to engage in self-reflection and to treat different perspectives and experiences with respect. Participation is voluntary.

events.description:
Decisive is the New Black is a 90-minute working session for creative professionals who are exhausted by the volume of decisions they face every week. It’s built around proprietary frameworks that turns three-day deliberations into clear decisions, without the guilt, the second-guessing, or becoming someone who says no – or yes – to everything.

The workshop is designed for high-achieving creatives: founders, directors, producers, designers, agency leaders, programmers, curators, and the executives behind them. People who built their careers by being capable, by saying yes, by figuring it out. People who eventually realise the strategy that got them here is quietly eating their energy and pulling them away from the work they want to be doing.

You’ll leave with the frameworks applied to real decisions you brought into the session, plus the language for the conversations where saying no feels impossible.

The workshop is led by Lindi Delight, a dual-certified Transformation Coach and Conference Programme Director for Most Wanted: Music in Berlin, with twenty years across the global creative industries. Her work is anchored in a simple principle: how you live is how you lead.

events.title: Shame & Sex: Writing Erotic Fiction and Overcoming Resistance
events.excerpt: A writing workshop on sexual shame, desire and the power of storytelling. The workshop creates a safe space to explore shame and intimacy through writing…
events.description:
I invite participants to explore, through writing, one of the most powerful emotions in our lives: shame, particularly sexual shame.

Ausgehend von meinem Roman „Schöne Scham“ Drawing on my novel "Schöne Scham" ("Beautiful Shame") and my upcoming non-fiction book, in which I explore desire, vaginismus, and societal expectations through my own story, I create a safe space where writing can be experienced as a tool for self-empowerment.

In my novel, I incorporated detailed sex scenes into the plot for the first time—deliberately not smooth or choreographed, but vivid, contradictory, and sometimes embarrassing. I am convinced that anyone who writes about sexuality bears a responsibility. Many readers look to texts for guidance, for an answer to the quiet, weighty question: "Am I normal?"

The workshop combines personal prompts with concrete writing exercises. It's not about provocation, but about honesty. Not about pornography, but about perspective. Not about perfection, but about intimacy.

Content & Schedule (60–90 minutes):

The exercises allow for different approaches—from autobiographical to fictional, from explicit to metaphorical. Each person decides for themselves how far they want to go. Texts do not have to be read aloud.

Target audience: Anyone interested in writing, readers, creative types, and people who want to explore desire, shame and intimacy, regardless of prior experience.

This workshop is intended as an invitation: writing can relieve pressure, open up new perspectives and reveal desires that lie beyond conventional expectations. Intimacy begins where perfection ends, and that is precisely where this course comes in.

A little about myself:

My name is Bianca Nawrath, An author and actress with Polish roots. Born in Berlin in 1997, I first appeared on camera at the age of 14 as the presenter of a youth programme. I made my acting debut in 2018. Since then, I have appeared alongside Judi Dench, Jürgen Vogel and Christian Ulmen, among others. My first novel, *Eat This Now, If You Love Me*, was published by Ecco Verlag in 2021, and most recently *Beautiful Shame* (2023) by Frankfurter Verlagsanstalt.

More about me and my thoughts on shame:

https://thisisafemsworld.de/bianca-nawrath/

events.title: Toxic Femininity and genuine Connection
events.excerpt: Right Here, Right Now – Toxic Femininity and Genuine Encounters Many of us today have a nuanced vocabulary for emotions, boundaries and social…
events.description:
Right Here, Right Now – Toxic Femininity and Genuine Encounter

Many of us today have a nuanced vocabulary for emotions, boundaries, and social dynamics—and yet we still find it difficult to remain truly present in our interactions with ourselves and others. Instead, we often fall back on learned roles and strategies: conformity, feigned closeness, emotional control, or constantly anticipating the needs of others.

In this space for exploration, Sophia Fritz and Christina Lehr from ehrlichleben combine brief insights into feminine and masculine influences with trauma-sensitive body exercises, reflection, and shared experiences. The starting point is the question of how connection becomes possible when we not only talk about our patterns but begin to perceive them in the present moment.

Together, we explore how shame, neediness, insecurity, or the desire for belonging influence our behavior—and why emotional sensitivity does not automatically lead to genuine closeness. How do we encounter one another beyond self-optimization, analysis, or social performance? What happens when we stop constantly curating ourselves?

This space is not intended as therapy, but as a communal space for shared experience. No prior knowledge is required, just openness and curiosity.

WIKABARETT offers a personal vision of contemporary cabaret. The lack of affection and social judgment are presented as mechanisms of contemporary alienation. Numbing through narcotization and junk food serve as anesthetics against existential discomfort and sexual repression.
